To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have constructed and expressed hRenalase coding sequence and its variant 2 in E. coli and have generated a polyclonal antirenalase antibody.

we have constructed and expressed the coding sequence of hRenal2 and have demonstrated that hRenal2 protein is recognized by anti-hRenal1 antibodies, suggesting that hRenalase 1 and hRenalase are functionally related.

the coding sequence of the renalase transcription variant 2 (hRenalase2) was constructed and expressed as a recombinant protein, and that the hRenalases 1 and 2 are similar proteins, as they are recognized by the same antibodies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the first description of a novel renalase protein variant, hRenalases2, its expression and purification in the prokaryotic system, and the development of a new tool for research of renalase function.

the development of the method for the construction of the full-length hRen1/2 coding sequence, its expression and purification in the prokaryotic system and the generation of polyclonl antibodies against the recombinant protein.
the development of the method of synthesis and purification of recombinant proteins, which is applicable for construction of coding sequence of various genes and their splice variants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presented approach is applicable to construction of coding sequences and expression of various proteins in E. coli.
the hRenalas2 protein is expressed in human tissues.
the presented method is an efficient tool for construction of full coding sequence of any protein, its purification, and generation of antibodies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hRenalases1 and 2 proteins are expressed in the prokaryotic system, and that hRenalase antibodies can be used for their detection.
the approach used for hRenalase is applicable for construction of full length coding sequences for other genes, their splice variants and their expression in the prokaryotic system.
hRenalase is a protein with multiple splice variants and multiple functions, and that the hRenalases are a family of proteins with different molecular weights, isoelectric points and functions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to construct coding sequences of various splice variants of the same gene and to express them as recombinant proteins in the prokaryotic system.
the hRenalases are expressed as a family of proteins, and the functions of the family members are not yet clear.
the approach we have developed can be applied to the synthesis of any protein sequence of interest.
